newsitem.title: CHINA: China Vitamin C cartel seeks better health.
newsitem.headline: China Vitamin C cartel seeks better health.

text.p: A cartel of Chinese vitamin C producers has called for unity to boost the health of a market plagued by tumbling prices and slumping profits, the official China Daily said on Monday.

The Chinese manufacturers had muscled their way to control almost one-third of world vitamin C supply but had been forced by slack demand to slash prices by almost 50 percent since last year, it said.

Meagre profits had forced half of China's vitamin C makers to cut production or to close down, but government departments were working to help the survivors stay in business, the newspaper quoted officials of the vitamin C trade association as saying.
"We are calling for unity among domestic vitamin C makers to hone our competitive edge and in the meantime deal with worsening market prospects," it quoted one official as saying.

The newspaper gave no details of how the trade body, described as a cartel, would respond to price-cutting from foreign pharmaceutical firms whose hold on the world market had been smashed in recent years by Chinese producers.
China's vitamin C exports totalled 20,000 tonnes, or 70 percent of national output, in 1995. World demand was 80,000 tonnes and growing by at best five percent a year, it said.

Mergers and consolidation among Chinese makers and producers were urgently needed to salvage the sector, it quoted an official of the Chamber of Commerce for Medicines and Health Care products as saying.
